_source: Shipped example obligation manifest for the ranked-choice tabulation project templates/evidence-records.example.json carries records for. It declares the complete required obligation set - one invariant and one system claim composing it - so the paired record set is complete: every id below has a record beside it. A project's manifest lives at .fv/obligations.json, and its bytes are what every record's bindings.obligation_manifest_hash binds, so editing this file (reformatting included) stales the evidence produced against it.
_consumers: Gate B (scripts/check_evidence_records.py) reads invariants[].id, witnesses[].id, and system_claims[] - each claim's depends_on and required_evidence. scripts/obligation_check.py reads the quint-facing half of the same file (intent_path, spec_dir, main_file, module, init, step, invariants[].name, invariants[].definition_sha256, transitions, bounds); those fields are omitted here so the example stays about the evidence set. Semantics: docs/dogfood-evidence.md.

invariants.name: inv_no_tied_elimination
invariants.statement: No candidate is eliminated while tied for the minimum tally

_witnesses_note: Empty on purpose: a witness declared here without a record would read as INCOMPLETE, and this example ships a complete record set. A real project declares its reachability witnesses here, each with its own record, and may name them in a system claim's depends_on.

system_claims.statement: Protocol model, proved tally core, and contract entry point agree on eliminated-candidate ordering

_system_claims_note: required_evidence names evidence tool IDs, matched against the `tool` of each execution in the claim's cohort: S1 PASSes only when quint, verus, and cargo-kani each appear as a PASS execution of S1's record. depends_on names declared invariants and witnesses only, never another claim, and those obligations still carry their own records - S1 passing does not discharge A1.
